api/HeroKit.Banking.CardNumberExtensions.summary: Class CardNumberExtensions Namespace HeroKit.Banking Assembly HeroKit.dll Contains extension methods for validating payment card numbers and detecting the card brand. public static class CardNumberExtensions Inheritance object CardNumberExtensions Inherited Members object.Equals(object) object.Equals(object, object) object.GetHashCode() object.GetType() object.MemberwiseClone() object.ReferenceEquals(object, object) object.ToString() Remarks Spaces and dashes are ignored. Any other non-digit character makes the number invalid. The checks cover format and the Luhn checksum. They do not confirm that a card exists. Methods GetCardBrand(string?) Detects the brand of a payment card from its prefix and length. public static CardBrand GetCardBrand(this string? value) Parameters value string The card number. Spaces and dashes are ignored. Returns CardBrand The detected brand, or Unknown if no brand matches or the input is not made of digits. Examples "4111111111111111".GetCardBrand(); // CardBrand.Visa "378282246310005".GetCardBrand(); // CardBrand.AmericanExpress Remarks The Luhn check is not required here. Use IsValidCardNumber(string?) for that. IsValidCardNumber(string?) Determines whether a string is a valid payment card number. public static bool IsValidCardNumber(this string? value) Parameters value string The card number to check. Spaces and dashes are ignored. Returns bool true if the number has 12 to 19 digits and passes the Luhn check; otherwise, false. Null or empty input returns false. Examples "4111 1111 1111 1111".IsValidCardNumber(); // true "4111111111111112".IsValidCardNumber(); // false

Spaces are ignored and lowercase letters are accepted. Returns string The formatted IBAN, or null if the input is not a valid IBAN. Examples "tr330006100519786457841326".FormatIban(); // "TR33 0006 1005 1978 6457 8413 26" GetBank(string?) Returns the bank of a valid IBAN from the bank directory of its country (Banks). public static Bank? GetBank(this string? value) Parameters value string The IBAN, with or without spaces. Returns Bank The bank, or null if the IBAN is invalid, its country has no bank directory or the bank code is unknown. Examples "TR33 0006 1005 1978 6457 8413 26".GetBank()?.Name; // null: bank code 00061 is not assigned "TR78 0006 2000 0000 0006 2950 05".GetBank()?.Name; // "Türkiye Garanti Bankası A.Ş." IsValidIban(string?) Determines whether a string is a valid IBAN (ISO 13616). Spaces are ignored and lowercase letters are accepted. public static bool IsValidIban(this string? value) Parameters value string The string to check. Returns bool true if the string is a valid IBAN; otherwise, false. Null or empty input returns false. Examples "TR33 0006 1005 1978 6457 8413 26".IsValidIban(); // true "TR330006100519786457841327".IsValidIban(); // false Remarks The check covers structure (country letters, check digits, alphanumeric BBAN, length 15 to 34) and the mod-97 checksum. For Turkey ("TR") the length must be 26 and the reserved fifth character must be '0'. NormalizeIban(string?) Normalizes a valid IBAN to uppercase without spaces. public static string? NormalizeIban(this string? value) Parameters value string The IBAN to normalize. Spaces are ignored and lowercase letters are accepted. CustomRule = 11 A rule from Rules rejected the upload; see Message. DangerousContent = 6 The content is a program or script, whatever the extension says. DangerousExtension = 2 The extension belongs to a program or script, for example ".exe", ".js" or ".php", or is in BlockedExtensions. DoubleExtension = 3 A program or script extension is hidden before the last extension, for example "invoice.php.jpg". EmptyContent = 5 The content is empty. ExtensionMismatch = 8 The content does not fit the extension. InvalidFileName = 1 The file name is empty, too long, starts or ends with a dot or space, or contains a path separator, a colon, a control character or another character Windows does not allow. None = 0 The upload passed every check. NotAllowed = 9 The type is not in AllowedTypes. TooLarge = 12 The file is longer than MaxLength. UnknownContent = 7 The content type could not be detected and AllowUnknownContent is false. UnknownExtension = 4 The extension is missing or unknown.

Examples var validator = new UploadValidator(new UploadPolicy { AllowedTypes = [FileTypes.Jpeg, FileTypes.Png] }); UploadCheckResult result = validator.Validate(file.OpenReadStream(), file.FileName); if (!result.IsSafe) return BadRequest(result.Message); Remarks The checks run as a chain, in this order, and the first rejection stops it: file name, program or script extension (also hidden as in "a.php.jpg"), empty content, MaxLength, program or script content, known extension, detected content and whether it fits the extension, AllowedTypes, macros in Office documents (also VBA projects in legacy DOC and XLS files), active content in SVG, then the rules in Rules. An instance is immutable and thread-safe; register one per policy as a singleton. The check does not replace a request size limit in the web server, generated file names, re-encoding images or virus scanning. Checks whether a string is a serial number of the Turkish chip identity card (T.C. Returns bool True if the value has the format of the chip identity card serial; otherwise false. Examples "A12B34567".IsValidIdCardSerial(); // true "a12b34567".IsValidIdCardSerial(); // false: upper case only Remarks The check is structural; the card serial has no check digit. The serial of the old paper identity card (nüfus cüzdanı) has another format and is not accepted. IsValidKepAddress(string?) Checks whether a string is a KEP (Kayıtlı Elektronik Posta) address: an e-mail address on a ".kep.tr" domain. public static bool IsValidKepAddress(this string? value) Parameters value string The address, for example "firma@hs01.kep.tr". Returns bool True if the value is an e-mail address whose domain ends with ".kep.tr"; otherwise false. Examples "firma@hs01.kep.tr".IsValidKepAddress(); // true "firma@example.com".IsValidKepAddress(); // false Remarks The check is structural: one "@", a local part without spaces and a domain such as "hs01.kep.tr". It does not check that the mailbox exists. IsValidMersis(string?) Checks whether a string is a valid MERSİS number (Central Registry Record System number of a Turkish company). public static bool IsValidMersis(this string? value) Parameters value string The number to check, for example "0879001756600379". Returns bool True if the value has 16 digits, starts with 0 and contains a valid VKN; otherwise false. Examples "0879001756600379".IsValidMersis(); // true "0879001756700379".IsValidMersis(); // false: the embedded VKN is invalid Remarks A MERSİS number has 16 digits: "0", the 10-digit VKN of the company and a 5-digit serial. The check is structural: it verifies the embedded VKN, not that the number is registered. IsValidTckn(string?) Checks whether a string is a valid Turkish identity number (T.C. Kimlik No, TCKN). public static bool IsValidTckn(this string? value) Parameters value string The number to check. ToTitleCase(string?, CultureInfo) Converts a string to title case with the casing rules of the given culture. public static string ToTitleCase(this string? value, CultureInfo culture) Parameters value string The string to convert. culture CultureInfo The culture whose casing rules are used, for example tr-TR for İ/ı. Returns string The title-cased string, or an empty string if value is null. Examples "istanbul ılıca".ToTitleCase(CultureInfo.GetCultureInfo("tr-TR")); // "İstanbul Ilıca" "HELLO WORLD".ToTitleCase(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture); // "Hello World" Remarks Words start after whitespace or a hyphen. The first letter of each word is upper-cased and the rest is lower-cased, so all-caps input is converted too (unlike ToTitleCase(string)). Truncate(this string? value, int maxLength, string ellipsis = "…") Parameters value string The string to shorten. maxLength int The maximum length of the result. ellipsis string The text appended when the string is cut. articles/collections-and-dates.html.title: Collections and dates | HeroKit
articles/collections-and-dates.html.summary: Collections and dates Collections using HeroKit.Enumerables; items.IsNullOrEmpty(); // null-safe; reads at most one element of a lazy sequence products.WhereIf(onlyInStock, p => p.Stock > 0); // filter only when the condition is true query.OrderBy(x => x.Id).Page(pageNumber: 2, pageSize: 20); // 1-based paging source.ToReadOnlyList(); // read-only copy WhereIf and Page also work on IQueryable<T>, so Entity Framework translates them to SQL. Dates using HeroKit.DateTimes; var date = new DateTime(2024, 2, 15, 13, 45, 0); date.StartOfMonth(); // 2024-02-01 00:00:00 date.EndOfMonth(); // 2024-02-29 23:59:59.9999999 date.StartOfWeek(); // Monday 2024-02-12 date.IsWeekend(); // false new DateTime(1990, 2, 15).Age(asOf: date); // 34 date.AsFileName("Monthly Report"); // "monthly-report-2024-02-15-13-45-00" Business days Business days and public holidays take a Country with a holiday calendar: using HeroKit.Globalization; var day = new DateOnly(2026, 3, 19); day.IsBusinessDay(Countries.Turkey); // true day.AddBusinessDays(1, Countries.Turkey); // 2026-03-23, skips the bayram and the weekend day.CountBusinessDays(new DateOnly(2026, 3, 27), Countries.Turkey); // business days after day, up to and including 27 March; a half day counts 0.5 new DateOnly(2026, 10, 29).IsPublicHoliday(Countries.Turkey); // true See Countries and languages for holidays, half days and how to add a calendar for another country. Results keep the DateTimeKind of the input. DateOnly overloads are available for week, month, weekend, range and age helpers.

articles/conversions.html.title: Conversions | HeroKit
articles/conversions.html.summary: Conversions Every conversion comes in two forms. Neither throws for null, empty or invalid input. Form Example On bad input Lenient ToX "abc".ToInt(-1) returns the default value Checked TryToX "abc".TryTo(out int n) returns false Parsing uses the invariant culture unless you pass a provider. Strings to values using System.Globalization; using HeroKit.Strings; // Any IParsable<T>: int, long, decimal, double, DateTime, DateOnly, TimeOnly, Guid, ... "42".To<int>(); // 42 "x".To(defaultValue: -1); // -1 "2026-03-07".To<DateOnly>(); // 2026-03-07 "1,5".To<decimal>(provider: CultureInfo.GetCultureInfo("tr-TR")); // 1.5 "42".TryTo(out int number); // true, number == 42 "abc".ToNullable<int>(); // null // Shortcuts "42".ToInt(); // 42 (also ToLong, ToShort) "2026-03-07".ToDateTime(); // 7 March 2026 "07.03.2026".ToDateTime(provider: CultureInfo.GetCultureInfo("tr-TR")); "yes".ToBoolean(trueText: "yes"); // true "SGVyb0tpdA==".FromBase64(); // bytes, or null if invalid Decimals Without a provider ToDecimal is flexible: a comma is the decimal separator when present, otherwise a dot is. "1.234,56".ToDecimal(); // 1234.56 "1234.56".ToDecimal(); // 1234.56 "1,234.56".ToDecimal(provider: CultureInfo.InvariantCulture); // strict: 1234.56 "abc".TryToDecimal(out decimal amount); // false Enums "friday".ToEnum<DayOfWeek>(); // DayOfWeek.Friday (name, ignoring case) "5".ToEnum<DayOfWeek>(); // DayOfWeek.Friday (defined number) "99".ToEnum(DayOfWeek.Monday); // DayOfWeek.Monday (not defined: default) "Sunday".TryToEnum(out DayOfWeek day); // true Objects using HeroKit.Objects; object cell = "42"; cell.ConvertTo<int>(); // 42 ((object)"abc").ConvertTo(-1); // -1 row["Count"].TryConvertTo(out int count); ConvertTo handles DBNull, nullable targets, enums and GUIDs from strings or 16-byte arrays.

articles/countries-and-languages.html.title: Countries and languages | HeroKit
articles/countries-and-languages.html.summary: Countries and languages HeroKit 3.0 does not add a new set of methods for every country. It has one set of methods that take a country or a language. Türkiye and the United States are built in. Other countries use the same methods once you describe them. The model Type What it holds Built in Country ISO code, name, language, currency and optional rules: phone numbers, vehicle plates, postal codes, national and tax ids, public holidays, regions, IBAN lengths Countries.Turkey, Countries.UnitedStates Language ISO code and optional rules: casing and sorting (TextRules), numbers in words (NumberSpeller) Languages.Turkish, Languages.English Currency ISO code, symbol, separators, unit names Currencies.TurkishLira, Currencies.USDollar All types are in the HeroKit.Globalization namespace. Türkiye-only checks (TCKN, VKN, e-invoice) are in HeroKit.Globalization.Turkey. using HeroKit.Globalization; "0532 123 45 67".IsValidPhone(Countries.Turkey); // true "34 ABC 123".IsValidVehiclePlate(Countries.Turkey); // true 1234.5m.ToCurrencyString(Currencies.TurkishLira); // "₺1.234,50" "istanbul".ToUpper(Languages.Turkish); // "İSTANBUL" Every rule of a country is optional. A method that needs a rule the country does not have throws NotSupportedException. None of these rules use ICU or the culture data of the operating system. The results are the same on every machine, also with InvariantGlobalization. Add your own country Implement the rule interfaces you need, create a Country and register it. As a Program.cs, the statements come first and the class after them: using HeroKit.Globalization; var testland = new Country("XT", "Testland", Languages.Turkish) { PhoneNumbers = new SixDigitPhoneRules(), }; Countries.Register(testland); "912345".IsValidPhone(testland); // true "912345".IsValidMobilePhone(testland); // true "912345".ToE164(testland); // "+999912345" "912345".FormatPhone(testland); // "912 345" public sealed class SixDigitPhoneRules : IPhoneNumberRules { public bool IsValid(string? value) => value is { Length: 6 } && value.All(char.IsAsciiDigit); public bool IsMobile(string? value) => IsValid(value) && value![0] == '9'; public string? ToE164(string? value) => IsValid(value) ? "+999" + value : null; public string? Format(string? value) => IsValid(value) ? $"{value![..3]} {value[3..]}" : null; } The other rule properties are VehiclePlates (IVehiclePlateRules), PostalCodes, NationalIds, TaxIds and IbanRules (IIdentifierRules), Holidays (IHolidayCalendar), Regions and Currency. Countries.Register also makes the country available to the validation attributes by its ISO code: [PhoneNumber("XT")] works after the country is registered. Countries.Get("XT"), Countries.TryGet and Countries.All read the registry. A new language works the same way: create new Language("xx", "Name") { TextRules = ..., NumberSpeller = ... } with your own ITextRules and INumberSpeller. United States Countries.UnitedStates, Languages.English and Currencies.USDollar use the same methods: using HeroKit.Globalization; var us = Countries.UnitedStates; "(212) 555-0123".IsValidPhone(us); // true "+1 212 555 0123".FormatPhone(us); // "(212) 555-0123" "212.555.0123".ToE164(us); // "+12125550123" "10001-1234".IsValidPostalCode(us); // true (ZIP or ZIP+4) "123-45-6789".IsValidNationalId(us); // true (SSN) "12-3456789".IsValidTaxId(us); // true (EIN; SSN and ITIN are also accepted) us.FindRegion("ca")?.Name; // "California" (FIPS code 6) new DateOnly(2026, 7, 2).AddBusinessDays(1, us); // 2026-07-06 (July 3 is the observed Independence Day) 1234.5m.ToCurrencyString(Currencies.USDollar); // "$1,234.50" 123.50m.ToCurrencyWords(Currencies.USDollar); // "one hundred twenty-three dollars and fifty cents" 2_500_340L.ToWords(Languages.English); // "two million five hundred thousand three hundred forty" Phone numbers follow the North American Numbering Plan: a 10-digit number whose area code and exchange start with 2–9, with an optional +1, 1 or 001 prefix. US numbers do not show whether a line is mobile, so IsValidMobilePhone accepts every valid number. SSN, ITIN and EIN checks are structural. They reject numbers that are never issued (for example SSN area 000, 666 or 900–999), but they cannot prove that a number was issued. Public holidays are the 11 federal holidays from 1986 on, with Juneteenth from 2021. A holiday on a Saturday is observed on the Friday before, a holiday on a Sunday on the Monday after. Observed days are separate entries named "… (observed)". State holidays are not included. Regions are the 50 states and the District of Columbia. FindRegion accepts the FIPS code, the USPS abbreviation or the name. Vehicle plates differ by state, so IsValidVehiclePlate(Countries.UnitedStates) throws NotSupportedException. English text rules use invariant casing. Languages.English.TextRules!.Comparer sorts case-insensitively and puts lower case first: apple, Apple, banana. Türkiye Identity and tax numbers using HeroKit.Globalization; using HeroKit.Globalization.Turkey; "10000000146".IsValidTckn(); // true (TCKN) "4840847211".IsValidVkn(); // true (VKN) "10000000146".IsValidNationalId(Countries.Turkey); // true (TCKN) "4840847211".IsValidTaxId(Countries.Turkey); // true: VKN or TCKN "0879001756600379".IsValidMersis(); // true: "0", VKN, 5-digit serial "firma@hs01.kep.tr".IsValidKepAddress(); // true: e-mail address on a .kep.tr domain "A12B34567".IsValidIdCardSerial(); // true: serial of the chip identity card These are checksum checks; IsValidMersis checks the VKN inside the MERSİS number. They confirm that a number is well formed, not that it is issued. Input must contain digits only. Step-by-step guides with the algorithms: TCKN, VKN. A validated TCKN value Tckn holds a TCKN that has passed the check. Validate once where the value enters the system, then pass Tckn instead of string: Tckn id = Tckn.Parse("10000000146"); // FormatException for an invalid number Tckn.TryParse(input, out Tckn checkedId); id.ToMaskedString(); // "10*******46" for logs public sealed record Customer(Tckn Id, string Name); // JSON: {"Id":"10000000146", ...}; an invalid number fails deserialization app.MapGet("/customers/{id}", (Tckn id) => ...); // minimal APIs bind it; an invalid number returns 400 Tckn implements IParsable<Tckn> and has a JSON converter (also for the System.Text.Json source generator and Native AOT) and a type converter for MVC model binding. default(Tckn) holds no number: IsEmpty is true. IBAN using HeroKit.Banking; var iban = "tr33 0006 1005 1978 6457 8413 26"; iban.IsValidIban(); // true iban.NormalizeIban(); // "TR330006100519786457841326" iban.FormatIban(); // "TR33 0006 1005 1978 6457 8413 26" "TR78 0006 2000 0000 0006 2950 05".GetBank()?.Name; // "Türkiye Garanti Bankası A.Ş." Countries.Turkey.Banks!.All; // 30 banks with their 5-digit EFT codes IBAN validation works for every country with the ISO 13616 mod-97 check. When a registered country has IbanRules, its length and fixed positions are checked too: Türkiye IBANs must have 26 characters. See the IBAN validation guide for the algorithm. GetBank reads the bank code of a valid IBAN (positions 5–9 for Türkiye) and looks it up in the bank directory of the country (Country.Banks). It returns null for an unknown code. The list follows the EFT codes of the Banks Association of Türkiye; open an issue when a bank is missing. Regions, plates and postal codes using HeroKit.Globalization; Countries.Turkey.FindRegion("34")?.Name; // "İstanbul" Countries.Turkey.FindRegion(6)?.Name; // "Ankara" Countries.Turkey.FindRegion("sanliurfa")?.Code; // 63 (case and diacritics ignored) Countries.Turkey.Regions.Count; // 81 Countries.Turkey.GetDistricts("istanbul").Count; // 39 Countries.Turkey.FindDistrict("istanbul", "kadikoy")?.Name; // "Kadıköy" Countries.Turkey.FindDistrict(1421)?.RegionCode; // 34 "34abc123".FormatVehiclePlate(Countries.Turkey); // "34 ABC 123" "06 A 1234".IsValidVehiclePlate(Countries.Turkey); // true "34 Q 1234".IsValidVehiclePlate(Countries.Turkey); // false: Q is not a plate letter "34710".IsValidPostalCode(Countries.Turkey); // true Regions is a list of Region(Code, Name). For Türkiye the regions are the 81 provinces. Districts holds the 973 districts (ilçe) as District(Code, Name, RegionCode) with their official MERNİS codes, in Turkish alphabetical order per province. Neighbourhoods and streets are not included: they are tens of thousands of rows and change often. Phone numbers "0532 123 45 67".ToE164(Countries.Turkey); // "+905321234567" "+905321234567".FormatPhone(Countries.Turkey); // "0532 123 45 67" "(0212) 555 12 34".IsValidPhone(Countries.Turkey); // true "0212 555 12 34".IsValidMobilePhone(Countries.Turkey); // false Accepted prefixes: +90, 0090, 90, 0 or none. The check is structural, not an operator or area-code allow-list. Public holidays and business days new DateOnly(2026, 10, 29).IsPublicHoliday(Countries.Turkey); // true (Cumhuriyet Bayramı) new DateOnly(2026, 10, 28).IsHalfDayHoliday(Countries.Turkey); // true (afternoon off) new DateOnly(2026, 3, 20).GetPublicHoliday(Countries.Turkey)?.Name; // "Ramazan Bayramı 1. Gün" new DateOnly(2026, 3, 19).AddBusinessDays(1, Countries.Turkey); // 2026-03-23, skips the bayram and the weekend new DateOnly(2026, 10, 26).CountBusinessDays(new DateOnly(2026, 10, 30), Countries.Turkey); // 2.5: 28 October is a half day foreach (PublicHoliday holiday in Countries.Turkey.Holidays!.GetHolidays(2026)) Console.WriteLine($"{holiday.Date:dd.MM.yyyy} {holiday.Name}{(holiday.IsHalfDay ? " (yarım gün)" : "")}"); Fixed holidays follow Law No. 2429. Ramazan and Kurban Bayramı dates come from the Diyanet calendar and are available for FirstSupportedYear–LastSupportedYear of the calendar (2022–2027). Other years throw instead of returning incomplete data. Business days are Monday to Friday without full-day holidays. A half day (arife and 28 October) is a business day for IsBusinessDay and AddBusinessDays, and counts as 0.5 in CountBusinessDays. BusinessDaysUntil (obsolete since 3.7.0) counts it as a full day. Administrative bridge days (idari izin) are announced case by case and are not built in. Add them, or your company's holidays, to a copy of the country: using HeroKit.Globalization; Country turkeyWithLeave = Countries.Turkey.WithAdditionalHolidays( [ new PublicHoliday(new DateOnly(2026, 5, 18), "İdari izin", IsHalfDay: false), new PublicHoliday(new DateOnly(2026, 12, 31), "Yılbaşı arifesi", IsHalfDay: true), ]); new DateOnly(2026, 5, 18).IsBusinessDay(turkeyWithLeave); // false: 18 May is added as administrative leave new DateOnly(2026, 5, 18).IsBusinessDay(Countries.Turkey); // true: Countries.Turkey itself does not change A day you add replaces a holiday on the same date. WithHolidays(calendar) swaps the whole calendar for your own IHolidayCalendar. Register the copy as a singleton and use it everywhere instead of Countries.Turkey. IsBusinessDay(country) is also available. A custom country gets all of these methods when it has an IHolidayCalendar. Today in Türkiye A server usually runs in UTC. Türkiye is 3 hours ahead of UTC, so from 00:00 to 03:00 Türkiye time (21:00 to 00:00 UTC on the previous day), DateTime.Today on the server still shows the previous day. Country.Today() uses the country's time zone: using HeroKit.Globalization; Countries.Turkey.Today(); // today's date in Türkiye Countries.Turkey.Now(); // e.g. 2026-10-19 01:30 +03:00 Countries.Turkey.Today().IsBusinessDay(Countries.Turkey); Countries.Turkey.Today(TimeProvider.System); // pass a fake TimeProvider in tests TimeZone is Europe/Istanbul. A country with more than one time zone (the United States) has no TimeZone, and Today() throws NotSupportedException. Turkish lira 1234.5m.ToCurrencyString(Currencies.TurkishLira); // "₺1.234,50" 1234.5m.ToCurrencyString(Currencies.TurkishLira, CurrencyStyle.Abbreviation); // "1.234,50 TL" 1234.5m.ToCurrencyString(Currencies.TurkishLira, CurrencyStyle.IsoCode); // "1.234,50 TRY" The currency carries its own separators, so the result does not depend on the current culture. Amounts in words 123.ToWords(Languages.Turkish); // "yüz yirmi üç" 1_001_000L.ToWords(Languages.Turkish); // "bir milyon bin" 123.50m.ToCurrencyWords(Currencies.TurkishLira); // "yüz yirmi üç Türk lirası elli kuruş" var euro = new Currency("EUR", "€", Languages.Turkish) { UnitName = "Euro", SubunitName = "sent" }; 10.20m.ToCurrencyWords(euro); // "on Euro yirmi sent" Casing and sorting without ICU "istanbul ılıca".ToTitleCase(Languages.Turkish); // "İstanbul Ilıca" "istanbul".ToUpper(Languages.Turkish); // "İSTANBUL" "IŞIK".ToLower(Languages.Turkish); // "ışık" "IŞIK".EqualsIgnoreCase("ışık", Languages.Turkish); // true "ISIK".EqualsIgnoreCase("isik", Languages.Turkish); // false: I is the capital of ı For other cultures use ToTitleCase(culture) and EqualsIgnoreCase(other, culture) from HeroKit.Strings. The Turkish comparers follow the Turkish alphabet (c, ç, g, ğ, ı, i, o, ö, s, ş, u, ü) without ICU. This also works in containers and apps that run with invariant globalization, where culture-based comparison does not follow the Turkish alphabet. using HeroKit.Globalization; var comparer = Languages.Turkish.TextRules!.Comparer; string[] names = ["Zeynep", "Çağla", "Ilgın", "İpek", "Cem", "Şule", "Oya", "Ömer", "Uğur", "Ümit", "Gül"]; Array.Sort(names, comparer); // Cem, Çağla, Gül, Ilgın, İpek, Oya, Ömer, Şule, Uğur, Ümit, Zeynep var sorted = customers.OrderBy(c => c.Name, comparer).ThenBy(c => c.City, comparer); var cities = new Dictionary<string, int>(Languages.Turkish.TextRules!.IgnoreCaseComparer) { ["İzmir"] = 35 }; cities.ContainsKey("izmir"); // true cities.ContainsKey("IZMIR"); // false: I is ı, not i Comparer sorts lower case first. IgnoreCaseComparer ignores case with the Turkish rules and can be used as a dictionary or hash set comparer. e-Fatura and e-Arşiv using HeroKit.Globalization.Turkey; "ABC2026000000001".IsValidGibInvoiceNumber(); // true "ABC2026000000000".IsValidGibInvoiceNumber(); // false: the sequence starts at 1 "51d3bb18-9650-4c8e-825d-5a7f845be630".IsValidEttn(); // true GibInvoiceNumber.TryParse("ABC2026000000001", out GibInvoiceNumber parsed); // true var invoice = GibInvoiceNumber.Create("ABC", 2026, 41); invoice.ToString(); // "ABC2026000000041" invoice.Next().ToString(); // "ABC2026000000042" A GİB invoice number has 16 characters: a series of 3 upper-case letters or digits (A–Z, 0–9), a 4-digit year (2000–2099) and a 9-digit sequence from 1. Create throws ArgumentException for an invalid part; Next throws InvalidOperationException when the sequence reaches 999,999,999. An ETTN is a non-empty UUID in the 8-4-4-4-12 format. The [GibInvoiceNumber] and [Ettn] attributes and the GibInvoiceNumber() and Ettn() FluentValidation rules are described in Form validation. QR code (karekod) if (GibInvoiceQrCode.TryParse(scannedText, out GibInvoiceQrCode? qr)) { qr.SellerTaxId; // "4840847211" qr.Number.ToString(); // "ABC2026000000001" qr.Date; // 2026-10-15 qr.PayableAmount; // 120.00 qr.VatAmounts[20m]; // 20.00 (VAT per rate) } TryParse reads the JSON text in the QR code of an e-Fatura or e-Arşiv invoice. It requires a valid seller and buyer VKN or TCKN ("11111111111" is accepted for e-Arşiv buyers without one), invoice number, ETTN and date. Amounts are optional; every field is also in Fields. It reads the text only and does not ask GİB whether the invoice exists.

articles/file-types.html.title: File types and safe uploads | HeroKit
articles/file-types.html.summary: File types and safe uploads HeroKit.FileTypes is a separate package. It has no dependencies and works with Native AOT. dotnet add package HeroKit.FileTypes Detect the type of a file using HeroKit.FileTypes; using FileStream stream = File.OpenRead(path); FileType? type = FileTypes.Detect(stream); // reads at most 16 KB and restores the position type?.MimeType; // "image/png" type?.Extension; // "png" type?.Category; // FileTypeCategory.Image Detection reads the magic bytes at the start of the file. About 70 types are built in: Group Types Images PNG, JPEG, GIF, WebP, BMP, TIFF, ICO, PSD, AVIF, HEIC, HEIF, JPEG XL, SVG Documents PDF, RTF, DOCX, XLSX, PPTX, DOCM, XLSM, PPTM, ODT, ODS, ODP, EPUB, legacy Office (OLE) Archives ZIP, 7z, RAR, gzip, bzip2, xz, Zstandard, tar Audio and video MP3, AAC, FLAC, Ogg, WAV, M4A, MIDI, MP4, M4V, MOV, 3GP, WebM, Matroska, AVI, MPEG, FLV Fonts WOFF, WOFF2, TTF, OTF Programs Windows executables, ELF, Mach-O, Java class and JAR, Android APK and DEX, WebAssembly, Windows shortcuts Other SQLite, Parquet, glTF binary Text JSON, XML, HTML, shell scripts with a #! line, plain text Some types need more than fixed bytes, and HeroKit handles them: Office and OpenDocument files are ZIP files. HeroKit reads the entry names (word/, xl/, ppt/) and the mimetype entry of OpenDocument and EPUB files, without decompressing anything. From a seekable stream it also reads the ZIP central directory at the end of the file (at most 1 MB), so large files are recognized too. From a span with only the first bytes, or from a stream that cannot seek, entries beyond the header are not seen and the result can be FileTypes.Zip. Macro-enabled Office files (DOCM, XLSM, PPTM) are recognized by their VBA project entry and have HasMacros set. MP4, MOV, M4A, 3GP, HEIC and AVIF share one container. HeroKit reads the brands of the ftyp box and never fails on several matches. WebM and Matroska, Java class files and Mach-O universal binaries share their first bytes. HeroKit reads the bytes that tell them apart. Text types are recognized by their start: { or [ for JSON, <?xml, <svg, <html. CSV, YAML and Markdown look like plain text, so they are detected as FileTypes.PlainText. DetectAll returns every match, for example DOCX and ZIP. Detect(ReadOnlySpan<byte>) works on bytes you already have; a longer span lets the ZIP detector see more entries. Extensions and MIME types FileTypes.GetMimeType("report.docx"); // "application/vnd.openxmlformats-officedocument.wordprocessingml.document" FileTypes.GetMimeType("unknown.xyz"); // "application/octet-stream" FileTypes.FromExtension(".JPEG")?.MimeType; // "image/jpeg" FileTypes.FromMimeType("image/x-icon")?.Extension; // "ico" (aliases are accepted) FileTypes.FromMimeType("application/json; charset=utf-8"); // FileTypes.Json Built-in file types Every built-in type is a static property of FileTypes that returns a FileType. FileTypes.BuiltIn lists all 89 of them in detection order. using HeroKit.FileTypes; FileType msi = FileTypes.Msi; // the same instance on every call msi.Name; // "Windows installer" msi.Category; // FileTypeCategory.Executable msi.MimeType; // "application/x-msi" msi.OtherMimeTypes; // ["application/x-ms-installer"] msi.Extensions; // ["msi", "msp"] msi.IsExecutable; // true: uploads of it are rejected msi.IsA(FileTypes.CompoundFile); // true: an MSI is an OLE compound file FileTypes.FromExtension("setup.msi") == FileTypes.Msi; // true FileTypes.FromMimeType("application/x-ms-installer") == FileTypes.Msi; // true FileTypes.Detect(msiBytes) == FileTypes.CompoundFile; // true: the content has no MSI-only signature FileTypes.ContentMatchesExtension(msiBytes, "setup.msi"); // true FileTypes.CheckUpload(msiBytes, "setup.msi").Rejection; // UploadRejection.DangerousExtension The getter is a static property: FileTypes.Msi always returns the same FileType, so compare with ==. msiBytes stands for the first bytes of an .msi file. Some formats share one container. Legacy Office files, Outlook messages and MSI installers are all OLE compound files, so their content detects as CompoundFile and the extension tells which one it is. The notes below say when this applies. FileType.Parent describes these links, and IsA follows them. Safe uploads var policy = new UploadPolicy { AllowedTypes = [FileTypes.Jpeg, FileTypes.Png, FileTypes.Pdf] }; UploadCheckResult result = FileTypes.CheckUpload(file.OpenReadStream(), file.FileName, policy); if (!result.IsSafe) return BadRequest(result.Message); CheckUpload follows the OWASP file upload advice. It rejects: Rejection Example InvalidFileName ../a.png, a.png:evil.exe, .htaccess, names with control characters or ending in a dot DangerousExtension .exe, .js, .php, .aspx, .html, web.config DoubleExtension invoice.php.jpg, photo.exe.png UnknownExtension no extension, or one HeroKit does not know EmptyContent an empty file TooLarge a file longer than MaxLength bytes (no limit by default) DangerousContent a program or script whatever the extension says, for example a Windows executable named photo.png UnknownContent content no detector recognizes (allow it with AllowUnknownContent) ExtensionMismatch a PDF named photo.png NotAllowed a type outside AllowedTypes ActiveContent SVG with script, event handlers, javascript: links, foreignObject, entity declarations or external references; Office documents with macros (DOCM, XLSM, or a legacy DOC or XLS with a VBA project) unless AllowMacros is true CustomRule one of your Rules The stream overload reads the whole SVG up to MaxSvgScanLength (1 MB) so a script at the end is found. A macro-enabled document disguised as .docx is rejected as ExtensionMismatch, also when the macro entry is at the end of a large file. Legacy Word and Excel files (DOC, XLS) have no separate macro type, so HeroKit reads their directory and rejects a file with a VBA project. Pass the whole file as a span, or a seekable stream; only the directory is read. Excel 4.0 macro sheets and PowerPoint 97-2003 macros are not found. A complete ASP.NET Core minimal API that uses UploadValidator and Tckn is in samples/HeroKit.Samples.WebApi. ASP.NET Core dotnet add package HeroKit.FileTypes.AspNetCore adds checks for IFormFile: using HeroKit.FileTypes; using HeroKit.FileTypes.AspNetCore; // Minimal APIs: a rejected file returns 400 (validation problem) before the handler runs. app.MapPost("/documents", (IFormFile file) => Results.Ok(file.GetSafeFileName())) .ValidateUploads(new UploadPolicy { AllowedTypes = [FileTypes.Pdf], MaxLength = 10 * 1024 * 1024 }); // MVC, Razor Pages and Blazor models public sealed class ProfileForm { [Required, AllowedFileTypes("jpg", "png", "webp", MaxLength = 5 * 1024 * 1024)] public IFormFile? Photo { get; set; } } // Anywhere var pdfOnly = new UploadPolicy { AllowedTypes = [FileTypes.Pdf] }; UploadCheckResult result = file.CheckUpload(pdfOnly); // or validator.Validate(file) with a singleton UploadValidator ValidateUploads also works on route groups and checks IFormFileCollection arguments. With FluentValidation, use RuleFor(x => x.Photo).SafeUpload(f => f.OpenReadStream(), f => f.FileName, policy) from HeroKit.FluentValidation. Size limit and safe names using HeroKit.FileTypes; // file is the uploaded IFormFile. var policy = new UploadPolicy { AllowedTypes = [FileTypes.Pdf], MaxLength = 10 * 1024 * 1024 }; // PDF up to 10 MB using Stream upload = file.OpenReadStream(); UploadCheckResult result = FileTypes.CheckUpload(upload, file.FileName, policy); if (!result.IsSafe) return Results.BadRequest(result.Message); // for example "The file is larger than 10485760 bytes." // Store under a generated name; keep the cleaned original name for display and downloads. string displayName = FileTypes.ToSafeFileName(file.FileName); // "rapor_.pdf" for "C:\temp\rapor?.pdf" string storedName = Guid.NewGuid().ToString("N") + Path.GetExtension(displayName); // Later, when the file is downloaded (storedFile is the stream of the stored file): return Results.File(storedFile, FileTypes.GetMimeType(displayName), fileDownloadName: displayName); MaxLength checks the length of a span, or of a stream that can seek. Also set the request size limit of the web server (for example [RequestSizeLimit] or Kestrel's MaxRequestBodySize), so a large upload is refused before it is read. ToSafeFileName drops any path, replaces characters that are not allowed in Windows file names with _, trims dots and spaces, guards Windows device names such as CON, and shortens the name to 255 characters. Letters of every language stay. With fileDownloadName, ASP.NET Core writes the Content-Disposition: attachment header and encodes non-ASCII names (filename*=UTF-8''...), so do not build that header by hand. The check is a first line of defense. Also limit the upload size, store files under generated names outside the web root, serve them with Content-Disposition: attachment where possible, and re-encode images or scan files when it matters. Dependency injection and your own registry The static FileTypes methods use the shared registry FileTypes.Default. For dependency injection, tests or per-tenant types, create instances: var registry = new FileTypeRegistry(); // the built-in types; new FileTypeRegistry(types) for only your list registry.Register(myType); // does not change FileTypes.Default builder.Services.AddSingleton(registry); builder.Services.AddSingleton(new UploadValidator(new UploadPolicy { AllowedTypes = [FileTypes.Pdf] }, registry)); public sealed class DocumentsController(UploadValidator validator) : ControllerBase { [HttpPost] public IActionResult Upload(IFormFile file) { UploadCheckResult result = validator.Validate(file.OpenReadStream(), file.FileName); return result.IsSafe ? Ok() : BadRequest(result.Message); } } Both types are thread-safe. UploadValidator runs its checks as a chain: each check is a small step with one job, and your IUploadRule instances are the last steps. Extensions in UploadPolicy.BlockedExtensions are always rejected, together with the extensions of program and script types; extend the default list with new HashSet<string>(UploadPolicy.DefaultBlockedExtensions) { "dwg" }. Add your own types and rules Register a type with one or more detectors. Registered types are checked before the built-in types, and their extensions and MIME types win. FileTypes.Register(new FileType("Sketch document", "application/x-sketch", FileTypeCategory.Document, "sketch") { Detectors = [new ZipEntryDetector("document.json")], Parent = FileTypes.Zip, }); FileTypes.Register(new FileType("Canon raw image", "image/x-canon-cr3", FileTypeCategory.Image, "cr3") { Detectors = [new IsoMediaDetector("crx ")], }); FileTypes.Register(new FileType("My format", "application/x-my-format", FileTypeCategory.Other, "myf") { Detectors = [new MagicNumber("4D 59 46 ?? 01"), MagicNumber.FromText("MYF2")], }); Detector Matches MagicNumber fixed bytes at an offset; ?? matches any byte ZipEntryDetector a ZIP entry name prefix, or an OpenDocument-style mimetype entry IsoMediaDetector ftyp brands of MP4-style files your class implement IFileTypeDetector.IsMatch(ReadOnlySpan<byte>) Add checks to uploads with IUploadRule. Rules run after the built-in checks: sealed class MinimumImageSizeRule : IUploadRule { public string? Validate(ReadOnlySpan<byte> header, string fileName, FileType? detectedType) => detectedType?.Category == FileTypeCategory.Image && header.Length < 100 ? "The image is too small." : null; } var policy = new UploadPolicy { Rules = [new MinimumImageSizeRule()] };

articles/getting-started.html.title: Getting started | HeroKit
articles/getting-started.html.summary: Getting started Install dotnet add package HeroKit HeroKit targets .NET 8 and .NET 10 and has no dependencies. Use Every helper is an extension method. Import the namespace of the area you need: Namespace What it covers HeroKit.Strings Checks, conversions, slugs, casing, truncating and masking HeroKit.Globalization Country, Language and Currency with Countries.Turkey, Languages.Turkish, Currencies.TurkishLira: phone numbers, plates, postal codes, regions, national and tax ids, holidays and business days, currency formatting, amounts in words, casing and sorting HeroKit.Globalization.Turkey Türkiye-only checks: TCKN, VKN, e-Fatura invoice numbers, ETTN HeroKit.Banking IBAN and card number validation HeroKit.Validation Form validation attributes: [Tckn], [Iban], [PhoneNumber("TR")], ... HeroKit.Enumerables Null-safe checks, conditional filters, paging HeroKit.DateTimes Formatting and date ranges HeroKit.Decimals Price rounding and VAT HeroKit.Objects, HeroKit.Types, HeroKit.Enums, ... Conversions and reflection helpers using HeroKit.Strings; "HeroKit extensions".ToSlug(); // "herokit-extensions" "42".ToInt(); // 42 "HeroKit extensions".Truncate(10); // "HeroKit e…" The country and language helpers take a Country or Language argument, so a new country needs no new methods. See Countries and languages. Conventions Bad input does not throw. Checks return false; conversions have a lenient ToX (default value) and a checked TryToX form; string helpers return null or an empty string as documented. Parsing is culture-invariant. Pass a CultureInfo when a culture matters, for example "07.03.2026".ToDateTime(provider: CultureInfo.GetCultureInfo("tr-TR")). Deprecated APIs are marked [Obsolete] with the replacement in the message and are removed only in the next major version. Upgrading from 1.x or 2.x? See Upgrading to 3.0.

articles/iban-validation.html.title: Validate an IBAN in C# (Turkish IBAN example) | HeroKit
articles/iban-validation.html.summary: Validate an IBAN in C# (Turkish IBAN example) The 3rd and 4th characters of an IBAN are check digits calculated from the rest of the number (ISO 13616, mod-97). Turkish IBANs have 26 characters. This page explains the algorithm, shows how to handle spaces and lower case in user input, and how to find the bank of an IBAN. HeroKit validates the IBANs of every country. Short answer using HeroKit.Banking; var iban = "tr33 0006 1005 1978 6457 8413 26"; iban.IsValidIban(); // true iban.NormalizeIban(); // "TR330006100519786457841326": store this iban.FormatIban(); // "TR33 0006 1005 1978 6457 8413 26": show this "TR78 0006 2000 0000 0006 2950 05".GetBank()?.Name; // "Türkiye Garanti Bankası A.Ş." dotnet add package HeroKit Structure of a Turkish IBAN Characters Example Meaning 1–2 TR Country code 3–4 33 Check digits 5–9 00061 Bank code (EFT code) 10 0 Reserved, always 0 11–26 0519786457841326 Account number (16 digits) The mod-97 rule Remove the spaces and convert letters to upper case. Move the first 4 characters to the end: 0006100519786457841326TR33. Replace each letter with a two-digit number: A = 10, B = 11 … Z = 35. T = 29, R = 27. If the resulting long number modulo 97 is 1, the IBAN is valid. The number is too long for long. Calculating the remainder digit by digit is enough; BigInteger is not needed. Plain C# without a library static bool IsValidTurkishIban(string? value) { string iban = (value ?? "").Replace(" ", "").ToUpperInvariant(); if (iban.Length != 26 || !iban.StartsWith("TR")) return false; int remainder = 0; foreach (char c in iban[4..] + iban[..4]) { if (char.IsAsciiDigit(c)) remainder = (remainder * 10 + (c - '0')) % 97; else if (char.IsAsciiLetterUpper(c)) remainder = (remainder * 100 + (c - 'A' + 10)) % 97; else return false; } return remainder == 1; } For Turkish IBANs, this code gives the same result as HeroKit's IsValidIban for 300,000 random numbers. HeroKit also accepts the IBANs of other countries (15 to 34 characters) and checks the national length where a country has IBAN rules. Common mistakes Rejecting spaces. Users copy IBANs from banking apps in groups of four. Remove the spaces and convert to upper case before the check. NormalizeIban does this and returns null for an invalid IBAN. Only using a regex. ^TR\d{24}$ does not catch a mistyped digit. The mod-97 check does. Calculating with long. With letters converted to numbers, a 26-character IBAN has 28 digits and does not fit in long. Calculate the remainder step by step. Taking a valid IBAN for an open account. The algorithm says the number is well formed. It does not say that the account is open or that the name matches. Only the bank's services can confirm that. Find the bank GetBank reads the bank code of a valid IBAN (characters 5–9) and looks it up in the EFT codes of the Banks Association of Türkiye: Bank? bank = "TR78 0006 2000 0000 0006 2950 05".GetBank(); bank?.Name; // "Türkiye Garanti Bankası A.Ş." bank?.Code; // "00062" It returns null for an unknown code. If a bank is missing, open an issue. ASP.NET Core form validation using HeroKit.Validation; public sealed class PaymentForm { [Required, Iban] public string? Iban { get; set; } } With FluentValidation (dotnet add package HeroKit.FluentValidation): RuleFor(x => x.Iban).NotEmpty().Iban(); Masking for logs using HeroKit.Strings; "TR330006100519786457841326".Mask(4); // "**********************1326" Related TCKN validation VKN validation Countries and languages: IBAN rules of other countries

articles/nullable-and-aot.html.title: Nullable and AOT | HeroKit
articles/nullable-and-aot.html.summary: Nullable and AOT Nullable annotations With nullable reference types, string means "never null" and string? means "can be null", and the compiler warns before a null value causes a NullReferenceException. HeroKit's annotations give the compiler this information for every method. Every public API is annotated. Null-check helpers tell the compiler about the result: string? input = GetInput(); if (input.IsNotNullOrEmpty()) Console.WriteLine(input.Length); // no warning: input is not null here Trimming and Native AOT What is Native AOT? A .NET app normally ships as intermediate code (IL). The runtime turns it into machine code while the app runs; this is just-in-time (JIT) compilation. With Native AOT (ahead-of-time), dotnet publish compiles the whole app to machine code in advance. The result is one native executable that: starts faster and uses less memory, runs on a machine without the .NET runtime. This matters most for containers, serverless functions, command-line tools and ASP.NET Core minimal APIs. The cost: the app cannot load or generate code at run time, and code the app does not use is removed (trimming). Code that depends on reflection can then fail at run time. A library is AOT compatible when it does not need these features, so publishing produces no warnings for it. You do not have to use Native AOT. HeroKit works the same in a normal .NET app. AOT compatibility only means that HeroKit does not stop you from choosing it. HeroKit and Native AOT The package is marked IsAotCompatible. CI publishes a test app with Native AOT on every pull request and fails on any trimming warning. A few reflection-based helpers cannot be fully trimmed. They carry [RequiresUnreferencedCode] or [RequiresDynamicCode], so you get a warning at the call site: TypesExtensions.GetExtensionMethods, GetExtensionMethod, GetRealType The Country, Language and Currency model is made of plain objects and interfaces. It does not use reflection. Conversions, enum helpers and TrySetConvertedValue are AOT-safe since 2.0: they use IParsable<T> and generic enum APIs instead of reflection. References Native AOT deployment overview (Microsoft Learn): what Native AOT is, its limitations and how to publish. ASP.NET Core support for Native AOT Trim self-contained deployments Introduction to AOT warnings and Prepare .NET libraries for trimming: what IsAotCompatible checks in a library.

articles/prices.html.title: Prices, VAT and cards | HeroKit
articles/prices.html.summary: Prices, VAT and cards using HeroKit.Decimals; 12.37m.RoundToStep(0.05m); // 12.35 12.30m.ToPsychologicalPrice(); // 12.99 100m.AddPercent(18); // 118 100m.IncludeVat(20); // 120 120m.ExcludeVat(20); // 100 120m.VatAmountFromGross(20); // 20 Cards using HeroKit.Banking; "4111 1111 1111 1111".IsValidCardNumber(); // true (length and Luhn) "4111111111111111".GetCardBrand(); // CardBrand.Visa troyCard.GetCardBrand(); // CardBrand.Troy (prefix 9792) "4111111111111111".Mask(); // "************1111" Brands: Visa, Mastercard, American Express, Discover, JCB and Troy. Currency formatting using HeroKit.Globalization; 1234.5m.ToCurrencyString(Currencies.TurkishLira); // "₺1.234,50" 1234.5m.ToCurrencyString(Currencies.TurkishLira, CurrencyStyle.Abbreviation); // "1.234,50 TL" 1234.5m.ToCurrencyString(Currencies.TurkishLira, CurrencyStyle.IsoCode); // "1.234,50 TRY" 123.50m.ToCurrencyWords(Currencies.TurkishLira); // "yüz yirmi üç Türk lirası elli kuruş" A Currency holds its own symbol, separators and unit names, so the output does not depend on the current culture. Create your own instance for other currencies, for example new Currency("EUR", "€", Languages.Turkish) { UnitName = "Euro", SubunitName = "sent" }. See Countries and languages. Reading amounts using HeroKit.Globalization; "₺1.234,56".ToAmount(Currencies.TurkishLira); // 1234.56 "1.234,56 TL".TryToAmount(Currencies.TurkishLira, out decimal a); // true, 1234.56 "1.5".TryToAmount(Currencies.TurkishLira, out _); // false: "." groups thousands "$1,234.56".ToAmount(Currencies.USDollar); // 1234.56 TryToAmount and ToAmount read text with the separators of a currency, with or without its symbol, abbreviation or ISO code, and with a leading sign. Group separators must split the whole part into groups of three digits, so a mistyped price is rejected instead of being read as a different number. The culture of the machine is not used. Barcodes using HeroKit.Barcodes; "8691234567890".IsValidGtin(); // true (EAN-13; GS1 Türkiye prefixes are 868 and 869) "96385074".IsValidGtin(); // true (EAN-8) IsValidGtin checks EAN-8, UPC-A, EAN-13 and GTIN-14 numbers with the GS1 check digit. Rounding VAT helpers return unrounded values. Pass decimals: 2 to round with MidpointRounding.AwayFromZero, the usual rule on invoices.

articles/strings.html.title: Strings | HeroKit
articles/strings.html.summary: Strings using System.Globalization; using HeroKit.Globalization; using HeroKit.Strings; // Checks string? name = null; name.IsNullOrEmpty(); // true, and the compiler knows name is not null when false ",,,".IsNullOrEmpty(','); // true: only separators // Slugs and casing "Çağdaş Şehir İstanbul".ToSlug(); // "cagdas-sehir-istanbul" "HeroKitExtensions".ToDashCase(); // "hero-kit-extensions" "HELLO WORLD".ToTitleCase(CultureInfo.InvariantCulture); // "Hello World" "istanbul ılıca".ToTitleCase(Languages.Turkish); // "İstanbul Ilıca" "ığüşöç".RemoveDiacritics(); // "igusoc" // Shortening and masking "HeroKit extensions".Truncate(10); // "HeroKit e…" "5321234567".Mask(); // "******4567" "0532 123 45 67".Mask(2); // "**** *** ** 67" "10000000146".MaskMiddle(2, 2); // "10*******46" "TR33 0006 1005 1978 6457 8413 26".MaskMiddle(4, 4); // "TR33 **** **** **** **** **13 26" "emre.akdemir@example.com".MaskEmail(); // "e***********@example.com" "Ayşe Nur Yılmaz".MaskName(); // "A*** N** Y*****" "HeroKit".Left(4); // "Hero" "HeroKit".Right(4); // "oKit" "TR33 0006\t1005".RemoveWhitespace(); // "TR3300061005" RemoveDiacritics uses a fixed character table, not Unicode normalization, so the result is the same on every system, also with invariant globalization. It covers Turkish, Latin-1 and common Central European letters ("Łódź" becomes "Lodz") and keeps other characters. Casing and comparison with the rules of a language (ToUpper, ToLower, ToTitleCase, EqualsIgnoreCase with Languages.Turkish) are described in Countries and languages. Truncate never splits a surrogate pair. Mask and MaskMiddle keep whitespace so formatted values keep their layout. Use the masking methods to keep personal data (KVKK, GDPR) out of logs and screens: MaskMiddle hides a value completely when it is too short to keep both ends.

articles/tckn-validation.html.title: Validate a Turkish identity number (TCKN) in C# | HeroKit
articles/tckn-validation.html.summary: Validate a Turkish identity number (TCKN) in C# The Turkish identity number (TC Kimlik No, TCKN) has 11 digits. The last two digits are check digits calculated from the first nine. This page explains the algorithm step by step, shows common mistakes, and shows the same check in one line with HeroKit. Short answer using HeroKit.Globalization.Turkey; "10000000146".IsValidTckn(); // true "10000000147".IsValidTckn(); // false: wrong check digit dotnet add package HeroKit Rules The number has exactly 11 digits. The first digit is not 0. 10th digit: take 7 times the sum of the digits at positions 1, 3, 5, 7 and 9, and subtract the sum of the digits at positions 2, 4, 6 and 8. The result modulo 10 is the 10th digit. 11th digit: the sum of the first 10 digits modulo 10 is the 11th digit. Example: 10000000146 Calculation Result Odd positions (1, 3, 5, 7, 9) 1 + 0 + 0 + 0 + 1 2 Even positions (2, 4, 6, 8) 0 + 0 + 0 + 0 0 10th digit (2 × 7 − 0) mod 10 4 ✓ 11th digit (2 + 0 + 4) mod 10 6 ✓ Plain C# without a library static bool IsValidTckn(string? value) { if (value is null || value.Length != 11 || value[0] == '0' || !value.All(char.IsAsciiDigit)) return false; int[] d = value.Select(c => c - '0').ToArray(); int odd = d[0] + d[2] + d[4] + d[6] + d[8]; int even = d[1] + d[3] + d[5] + d[7]; int tenth = ((odd * 7 - even) % 10 + 10) % 10; // % can return a negative number in C# int eleventh = (odd + even + tenth) % 10; return d[9] == tenth && d[10] == eleventh; } This code gives the same result as HeroKit's IsValidTckn for 300,000 random numbers. Common mistakes Negative modulo. odd * 7 - even can be negative. In C#, -3 % 10 is -3, not 7. Without + 10) % 10, valid numbers are rejected. Storing it as a number. Do not store a TCKN as long or int. It is an identifier, not a quantity. Keep it as a string. Only checking the length or a regex. ^\d{11}$ does not catch a mistyped digit. The check digits do. Taking a well-formed number for a real person. The algorithm says the number is well formed, not that it is issued. To verify a person, use the service of the General Directorate of Population and Citizenship Affairs (NVİ) with the name, surname and birth year. Writing it to logs. A TCKN is personal data under KVKK, the Turkish data protection law. Mask it in logs and on screens (see below). ASP.NET Core form validation using HeroKit.Validation; public sealed class CustomerForm { [Required, Tckn] public string? IdentityNumber { get; set; } } With FluentValidation (dotnet add package HeroKit.FluentValidation): RuleFor(x => x.IdentityNumber).NotEmpty().Tckn(); A validated value type: Tckn Validate the number once where it enters the system, then pass Tckn instead of string: Tckn id = Tckn.Parse("10000000146"); // FormatException for an invalid number if (Tckn.TryParse(input, out Tckn checkedId)) { /* ... */ } public sealed record Customer(Tckn Id, string Name); // JSON: {"Id":"10000000146"} app.MapGet("/customers/{id}", (Tckn id) => Results.Ok(id)); // an invalid number returns 400 Masking for logs using HeroKit.Strings; Tckn.Parse("10000000146").ToMaskedString(); // "10*******46" "10000000146".MaskMiddle(2, 2); // "10*******46" Test numbers 10000000146 is a valid test number and does not belong to a real person. Generate more test numbers with the rules above. Do not put real people's numbers into test data. Related VKN validation: the tax number of companies. Sole proprietors use their TCKN as tax number; accept both with IsValidTaxId(Countries.Turkey). IBAN validation Form validation: every validation attribute

Amounts, currency and words 2.x 3.0 123.ToTurkishWords() 123.ToWords(Languages.Turkish) amount.ToTurkishCurrencyWords() amount.ToCurrencyWords(Currencies.TurkishLira) amount.ToTurkishCurrencyWords("Euro", "sent") amount.ToCurrencyWords(new Currency("EUR", "€", Languages.Turkish) { UnitName = "Euro", SubunitName = "sent" }) amount.ToTurkishLira() amount.ToCurrencyString(Currencies.TurkishLira) amount.ToTurkishLira(TurkishLiraFormat.Code) amount.ToCurrencyString(Currencies.TurkishLira, CurrencyStyle.Abbreviation) ("1.234,50 TL") — CurrencyStyle.IsoCode ("1.234,50 TRY") Public holidays and business days 2.x 3.0 TurkishHolidays.GetHolidays(2026) Countries.Turkey.Holidays!.GetHolidays(2026) date.IsPublicHolidayTr() date.IsPublicHoliday(Countries.Turkey) date.IsHalfDayHolidayTr() date.IsHalfDayHoliday(Countries.Turkey) date.GetPublicHolidayTr() date.GetPublicHoliday(Countries.Turkey) date.IsBusinessDayTr() date.IsBusinessDay(Countries.Turkey) date.AddBusinessDaysTr(n) date.AddBusinessDays(n, Countries.Turkey) date.BusinessDaysUntilTr(end) date.CountBusinessDays(end, Countries.Turkey) (3.7.0+, half days count 0.5) Casing and text 2.x 3.0 value.ToTitleCaseTr() value.ToTitleCase(Languages.Turkish) value.EqualsTr(other) value.EqualsIgnoreCase(other, Languages.Turkish) value.RemoveAccent() value.RemoveDiacritics() value.ClearTurkishChars() value.RemoveDiacritics() RemoveDiacritics uses a fixed character table, so it gives the same result on every system. It also covers Latin-1 and common Central European letters. Validation attributes 2.x 3.0 [TurkishPhone], [TurkishPhone(MobileOnly = true)] [PhoneNumber("TR")], [PhoneNumber("TR", MobileOnly = true)] [PlateTr] [VehiclePlate("TR")] [PostalCodeTr] [PostalCode("TR")] [TaxIdTr] [TaxId("TR")] — [NationalId("TR")] [Tckn], [Vkn], [Iban], [CardNumber] unchanged FluentValidation 2.x 3.0 TurkishPhone(mobileOnly) PhoneNumber(Countries.Turkey, mobileOnly) PlateTr() VehiclePlate(Countries.Turkey) PostalCodeTr() PostalCode(Countries.Turkey) TaxIdTr() TaxId(Countries.Turkey) — NationalId(Countries.Turkey) Tckn(), Vkn(), Iban(), CardNumber() unchanged New in 3.0 These did not exist in a released version: e-Fatura and e-Arşiv: GibInvoiceNumber (TryParse, Create, Next), IsValidGibInvoiceNumber, IsValidEttn, the [GibInvoiceNumber] and [Ettn] attributes and the GibInvoiceNumber() and Ettn() FluentValidation rules. They work with invariant globalization. Casing: ToUpper(Languages.Turkish) and ToLower(Languages.Turkish). Your own country, language or currency: new Country(...), Countries.Register, new Language(...), new Currency(...). Update checklist Replace using HeroKit.Turkish; with using HeroKit.Globalization; and add using HeroKit.Globalization.Turkey; where you call IsValidTckn or IsValidVkn. Rename the calls with the tables above. The compiler lists every old name. Replace the country attributes and FluentValidation rules. From 1.x Apply these changes first, then the From 2.x tables. HeroKit 2.0 applies one error policy to every conversion, makes names consistent and removes helpers that were obsolete or duplicated .NET. Most changes are renames that the compiler points out. articles/validation.html.title: Form validation | HeroKit
articles/validation.html.summary: Form validation DataAnnotations attributes for the HeroKit validators. They work with ASP.NET Core model validation, Blazor's DataAnnotationsValidator, minimal API filters and Validator.TryValidateObject. using System.ComponentModel.DataAnnotations; using HeroKit.Validation; public sealed class Customer { [Required, Tckn] public string? IdentityNumber { get; set; } [TaxId("TR")] public string? TaxId { get; set; } [Iban] public string? Iban { get; set; } [PhoneNumber("TR", MobileOnly = true, ErrorMessage = "Cep telefonu geçersiz.")] public string? Mobile { get; set; } [PostalCode("TR")] public string? PostalCode { get; set; } [VehiclePlate("TR")] public string? Plate { get; set; } [CardNumber] public string? Card { get; set; } [GibInvoiceNumber] public string? InvoiceNumber { get; set; } [Ettn] public string? Ettn { get; set; } } Attribute Checks [Tckn] Turkish identity number checksum [Vkn] Turkish tax number checksum [Iban] ISO 13616 mod-97; national length where a country has IBAN rules (TR: 26) [CardNumber] Length and Luhn [GibInvoiceNumber] e-Fatura / e-Arşiv invoice number in the GİB format, for example ABC2026000000001 [Ettn] ETTN: a non-empty UUID in the 8-4-4-4-12 format [KepAddress] KEP address: an e-mail address on a .kep.tr domain [IdCardSerial] Chip identity card serial number, for example A12B34567 [Mersis] MERSİS number: "0", a valid VKN and a 5-digit serial [Gtin] Barcode number (EAN-8, UPC-A, EAN-13, GTIN-14) with the GS1 check digit [PhoneNumber("TR")] Phone number of a country; MobileOnly = true for mobiles [VehiclePlate("TR")] Vehicle plate of a country [PostalCode("TR")] Postal code of a country (TR: 5 digits, valid province prefix) [NationalId("TR")] National identity number of a country (TR: TCKN) [TaxId("TR")] Tax identifier of a country (TR: VKN or TCKN) The country attributes take an ISO 3166-1 alpha-2 code. The country is looked up in Countries when a value is validated, so a country you add with Countries.Register works too. See Countries and languages. A country without the needed rules throws NotSupportedException. FluentValidation The separate HeroKit.FluentValidation package adds the same checks as FluentValidation rules. The core package stays dependency-free. dotnet add package HeroKit.FluentValidation using FluentValidation; using HeroKit.FluentValidation; using HeroKit.Globalization; public sealed class CustomerValidator : AbstractValidator<Customer> { public CustomerValidator() { RuleFor(x => x.IdentityNumber).NotEmpty().Tckn(); RuleFor(x => x.Iban).Iban(); RuleFor(x => x.Mobile).PhoneNumber(Countries.Turkey, mobileOnly: true); RuleFor(x => x.Plate).VehiclePlate(Countries.Turkey); RuleFor(x => x.InvoiceNumber).GibInvoiceNumber(); } } Rules: Tckn, Vkn, Iban, CardNumber, GibInvoiceNumber, Ettn, Mersis, Gtin, KepAddress, IdCardSerial, and the country rules PhoneNumber(country, mobileOnly), VehiclePlate(country), PostalCode(country), NationalId(country), TaxId(country). Messages use {PropertyName}; replace them with WithMessage. Notes Null and empty values are valid, so optional fields stay optional. Add [Required] to require a value. Default messages are English and include the field name; set ErrorMessage or resource properties to localize them.

articles/vkn-validation.html.title: Validate a Turkish tax number (VKN) in C# | HeroKit
articles/vkn-validation.html.summary: Validate a Turkish tax number (VKN) in C# The Turkish tax number (Vergi Kimlik Numarası, VKN) has 10 digits. The last digit is a check digit calculated from the first nine. Companies use a VKN. Sole proprietors use the owner's identity number (TCKN) as tax number. This page explains the algorithm and shows a check that accepts both. Short answer using HeroKit.Globalization; using HeroKit.Globalization.Turkey; "4840847211".IsValidVkn(); // true "4840847212".IsValidVkn(); // false "10000000146".IsValidTaxId(Countries.Turkey); // true: sole proprietor, TCKN "4840847211".IsValidTaxId(Countries.Turkey); // true: company, VKN dotnet add package HeroKit Rules The number has exactly 10 digits. For each of the first 9 digits, with p the position (1–9): a = (digit + 10 − p) mod 10 b = (a × 2^(10 − p)) mod 9 if a is not zero and b is zero, b = 9. Add up all b values. The 10th digit is (10 − sum mod 10) mod 10. Example: 4840847211 Position Digit a 2^(10 − p) b 1 4 3 512 6 2 8 6 256 6 3 4 1 128 2 4 0 6 64 6 5 8 3 32 6 6 4 8 16 2 7 7 0 8 0 8 2 4 4 7 9 1 2 2 4 The sum is 39. The check digit is (10 − 9) mod 10 = 1, which is the last digit, so the number is valid. Plain C# without a library static bool IsValidVkn(string? value) { if (value is null || value.Length != 10 || !value.All(char.IsAsciiDigit)) return false; int sum = 0; for (int i = 0; i < 9; i++) // i = position − 1 { int a = (value[i] - '0' + 9 - i) % 10; int b = a * (1 << (9 - i)) % 9; // 1 << n = 2^n if (a != 0 && b == 0) b = 9; sum += b; } return (10 - sum % 10) % 10 == value[9] - '0'; } This code gives the same result as HeroKit's IsValidVkn for 300,000 random numbers. Common mistakes Missing the 9 rule. When a is not zero and b is zero, b must be 9. Without this rule, some valid numbers are rejected. Rejecting sole proprietors. If an invoice or customer form accepts only a VKN, sole proprietors cannot enter their TCKN. Use IsValidTaxId(Countries.Turkey) or [TaxId("TR")] for that field. Storing it as a number. A VKN can start with 0. Stored as long, the leading zero is lost. Use string. Taking a well-formed number for a registered taxpayer. The algorithm says the number is well formed. It does not say that a taxpayer with this number is registered. Use the services of the Revenue Administration (GİB) for that. ASP.NET Core form validation using HeroKit.Validation; public sealed class InvoiceForm { [Required, TaxId("TR")] // VKN or TCKN public string? TaxNumber { get; set; } [Vkn] // VKN only public string? CompanyTaxNumber { get; set; } } With FluentValidation (dotnet add package HeroKit.FluentValidation): RuleFor(x => x.TaxNumber).NotEmpty().TaxId(Countries.Turkey); RuleFor(x => x.CompanyTaxNumber).Vkn(); MERSİS number The 16-digit MERSİS number is "0", the company's VKN and a 5-digit serial: "0879001756600379".IsValidMersis(); // true Related TCKN validation IBAN validation Form validation: every validation attribute

tr/articles/conversions.html.summary: Dönüşümler Her dönüşümün iki biçimi vardır. İkisi de null, boş ya da geçersiz girdide istisna fırlatmaz. Biçim Örnek Hatalı girdide Toleranslı ToX "abc".ToInt(-1) varsayılan değeri döner Denetimli TryToX "abc".TryTo(out int n) false döner Bir provider vermezseniz ayrıştırma değişmez kültürü (invariant culture) kullanır. Metinden değere using System.Globalization; using HeroKit.Strings; // Herhangi bir IParsable<T>: int, long, decimal, double, DateTime, DateOnly, TimeOnly, Guid, ... "42".To<int>(); // 42 "x".To(defaultValue: -1); // -1 "2026-03-07".To<DateOnly>(); // 2026-03-07 "1,5".To<decimal>(provider: CultureInfo.GetCultureInfo("tr-TR")); // 1.5 "42".TryTo(out int number); // true, number == 42 "abc".ToNullable<int>(); // null // Kısayollar "42".ToInt(); // 42 (ToLong ve ToShort da var) "2026-03-07".ToDateTime(); // 7 Mart 2026 "07.03.2026".ToDateTime(provider: CultureInfo.GetCultureInfo("tr-TR")); "yes".ToBoolean(trueText: "yes"); // true "SGVyb0tpdA==".FromBase64(); // bayt dizisi, geçersizse null Decimal değerler Provider olmadan ToDecimal esnektir: virgül varsa ondalık ayırıcı virgüldür, yoksa noktadır. "1.234,56".ToDecimal(); // 1234.56 "1234.56".ToDecimal(); // 1234.56 "1,234.56".ToDecimal(provider: CultureInfo.InvariantCulture); // katı: 1234.56 "abc".TryToDecimal(out decimal amount); // false Enum değerleri "friday".ToEnum<DayOfWeek>(); // DayOfWeek.Friday (ad, büyük-küçük harf yok sayılır) "5".ToEnum<DayOfWeek>(); // DayOfWeek.Friday (tanımlı sayı) "99".ToEnum(DayOfWeek.Monday); // DayOfWeek.Monday (tanımlı değil: varsayılan) "Sunday".TryToEnum(out DayOfWeek day); // true Nesneler using HeroKit.Objects; object cell = "42"; cell.ConvertTo<int>(); // 42 ((object)"abc").ConvertTo(-1); // -1 row["Count"].TryConvertTo(out int count); ConvertTo; DBNull, null olabilen hedefleri, enum değerlerini ve metinden ya da 16 baytlık dizilerden GUID'leri işler.

tr/articles/countries-and-languages.html.title: Ülkeler ve diller | HeroKit
tr/articles/countries-and-languages.html.summary: Ülkeler ve diller HeroKit 3.0 her ülke için ayrı bir metot kümesi eklemez. Ülke ya da dil alan tek bir metot kümesi vardır. Türkiye ve ABD hazır gelir. Diğer ülkeler, tanımladığınız anda aynı metotları kullanır. Model Tip Ne tutar Hazır olan Country ISO kodu, ad, dil, para birimi ve isteğe bağlı kurallar: telefon numaraları, araç plakaları, posta kodları, kimlik ve vergi numaraları, resmî tatiller, bölgeler, IBAN uzunlukları Countries.Turkey, Countries.UnitedStates Language ISO kodu ve isteğe bağlı kurallar: harf büyüklüğü ve sıralama (TextRules), yazıyla sayı (NumberSpeller) Languages.Turkish, Languages.English Currency ISO kodu, simge, ayırıcılar, birim adları Currencies.TurkishLira, Currencies.USDollar Bütün tipler HeroKit.Globalization namespace'indedir. Yalnızca Türkiye'ye ait kontroller (TCKN, VKN, e-fatura) HeroKit.Globalization.Turkey içindedir. using HeroKit.Globalization; "0532 123 45 67".IsValidPhone(Countries.Turkey); // true "34 ABC 123".IsValidVehiclePlate(Countries.Turkey); // true 1234.5m.ToCurrencyString(Currencies.TurkishLira); // "₺1.234,50" "istanbul".ToUpper(Languages.Turkish); // "İSTANBUL" Bir ülkenin her kuralı isteğe bağlıdır. Ülkede olmayan bir kurala ihtiyaç duyan metot NotSupportedException fırlatır. Bu kuralların hiçbiri ICU'yu ya da işletim sisteminin kültür verisini kullanmaz. Sonuç her makinede aynıdır; InvariantGlobalization açıkken de. Kendi ülkenizi ekleyin İhtiyacınız olan kural arayüzlerini uygulayın, bir Country oluşturun ve kaydedin. Program.cs olarak yazarken önce ifadeler, ardından sınıf gelir: using HeroKit.Globalization; var testland = new Country("XT", "Testland", Languages.Turkish) { PhoneNumbers = new SixDigitPhoneRules(), }; Countries.Register(testland); "912345".IsValidPhone(testland); // true "912345".IsValidMobilePhone(testland); // true "912345".ToE164(testland); // "+999912345" "912345".FormatPhone(testland); // "912 345" public sealed class SixDigitPhoneRules : IPhoneNumberRules { public bool IsValid(string? value) => value is { Length: 6 } && value.All(char.IsAsciiDigit); public bool IsMobile(string? value) => IsValid(value) && value![0] == '9'; public string? ToE164(string? value) => IsValid(value) ? "+999" + value : null; public string? Format(string? value) => IsValid(value) ? $"{value![..3]} {value[3..]}" : null; } Diğer kural özellikleri: VehiclePlates (IVehiclePlateRules), PostalCodes, NationalIds, TaxIds ve IbanRules (IIdentifierRules), Holidays (IHolidayCalendar), Regions ve Currency. Countries.Register, ülkeyi doğrulama özniteliklerine ISO koduyla da açar: ülke kaydedildikten sonra [PhoneNumber("XT")] çalışır. Kaydı Countries.Get("XT"), Countries.TryGet ve Countries.All okur. Yeni bir dil de aynı şekilde eklenir: kendi ITextRules ve INumberSpeller uygulamalarınızla new Language("xx", "Ad") { TextRules = ..., NumberSpeller = ... } oluşturun. Amerika Birleşik Devletleri Countries.UnitedStates, Languages.English ve Currencies.USDollar aynı metotlarla çalışır: using HeroKit.Globalization; var us = Countries.UnitedStates; "(212) 555-0123".IsValidPhone(us); // true "+1 212 555 0123".FormatPhone(us); // "(212) 555-0123" "212.555.0123".ToE164(us); // "+12125550123" "10001-1234".IsValidPostalCode(us); // true (ZIP ya da ZIP+4) "123-45-6789".IsValidNationalId(us); // true (SSN) "12-3456789".IsValidTaxId(us); // true (EIN; SSN ve ITIN de kabul edilir) us.FindRegion("ca")?.Name; // "California" (FIPS kodu 6) new DateOnly(2026, 7, 2).AddBusinessDays(1, us); // 2026-07-06 (3 Temmuz, Bağımsızlık Günü'nün resmî tatil günü) 1234.5m.ToCurrencyString(Currencies.USDollar); // "$1,234.50" 123.50m.ToCurrencyWords(Currencies.USDollar); // "one hundred twenty-three dollars and fifty cents" 2_500_340L.ToWords(Languages.English); // "two million five hundred thousand three hundred forty" Telefon numaraları Kuzey Amerika Numaralandırma Planı'na uyar: alan kodu ve santral kodu 2–9 ile başlayan 10 haneli numara; isteğe bağlı +1, 1 ya da 001 öneki. ABD numaraları hattın mobil olup olmadığını göstermez; bu yüzden IsValidMobilePhone her geçerli numarayı kabul eder. SSN, ITIN ve EIN kontrolleri yapısaldır. Hiç verilmeyen numaraları (ör. SSN alan kodu 000, 666 ya da 900–999) reddeder, ama numaranın gerçekten verildiğini kanıtlamaz. Resmî tatiller 1986'dan itibaren 11 federal tatildir; Juneteenth 2021'den itibaren eklenir. Cumartesiye gelen tatil önceki cuma, pazara gelen tatil sonraki pazartesi kullanılır. Bu günler "… (observed)" adıyla ayrı kayıttır. Eyalet tatilleri dahil değildir. Bölgeler 50 eyalet ve District of Columbia'dır. FindRegion FIPS kodunu, USPS kısaltmasını ya da adı kabul eder. Araç plakaları eyalete göre değişir; bu yüzden IsValidVehiclePlate(Countries.UnitedStates) NotSupportedException fırlatır. İngilizce metin kuralları değişmez (invariant) harf dönüşümü kullanır. Languages.English.TextRules!.Comparer büyük/küçük harfe bakmadan sıralar, eşitlikte küçük harfi öne koyar: apple, Apple, banana. Türkiye Kimlik ve vergi numaraları using HeroKit.Globalization; using HeroKit.Globalization.Turkey; "10000000146".IsValidTckn(); // true (TCKN) "4840847211".IsValidVkn(); // true (VKN) "10000000146".IsValidNationalId(Countries.Turkey); // true (TCKN) "4840847211".IsValidTaxId(Countries.Turkey); // true: VKN veya TCKN "0879001756600379".IsValidMersis(); // true: "0", VKN, 5 haneli sıra no "firma@hs01.kep.tr".IsValidKepAddress(); // true: .kep.tr alan adlı e-posta adresi "A12B34567".IsValidIdCardSerial(); // true: çipli kimlik kartı seri no Bunlar sağlama toplamı kontrolleridir; IsValidMersis MERSİS numarasının içindeki VKN'yi kontrol eder. Bir numaranın biçiminin doğru olduğunu gösterir; numaranın verilmiş olduğunu göstermez. Girdi yalnızca rakam içermelidir. Algoritmaları adım adım anlatan rehberler: TCKN, VKN. Doğrulanmış TCKN değeri Tckn, kontrolden geçmiş bir TCKN tutar. Değer sisteme girdiği yerde bir kez doğrulayın, sonra string yerine Tckn taşıyın: Tckn id = Tckn.Parse("10000000146"); // geçersiz numarada FormatException Tckn.TryParse(input, out Tckn checkedId); id.ToMaskedString(); // loglar için "10*******46" public sealed record Customer(Tckn Id, string Name); // JSON: {"Id":"10000000146", ...}; geçersiz numara deserialize edilmez app.MapGet("/customers/{id}", (Tckn id) => ...); // minimal API bağlar; geçersiz numara 400 döner Tckn, IParsable<Tckn> uygular; JSON dönüştürücüsü (System.Text.Json kaynak üreticisi ve Native AOT dahil) ve MVC model bağlama için tip dönüştürücüsü vardır. default(Tckn) numara tutmaz: IsEmpty true'dur.
